newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end ahead, await futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end ahead, await futures expiry.

text.p: Austrian shares ended largely higher across the board on Monday, but traders said the market was steeped in a wait-and-see mood ahead of the expiry of futures and options on Friday and the EU summit in Amsterdam.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips gained 5.68 points, or 0.44 percent, to 1,307.97 points with 15 shares advancing, five falling, and one unchanged.
Traders see the ATX remaining hemmed into its narrow trading range around 1,300 points.

"The ATX is currently pretty firmly squeezed in between 1,280 and 1,320 points," said one, adding that some players seemed to be trying to pin the ATX down to 1,300 points for the futures expiry on Friday.
Sentiment remains buoyant, emboldened by technical charts which show the formation of a triangle between 1,290 and 1,310 points on the ATX, raising hopes of an upward trend.
"But everyone's waiting for a stimulus," said a trader.
The day's top performing ATX stock was cartonboard maker Mayr-Melnhof, up 1.6 percent, or 9.9 schillings at 630.
Hosiery maker Wolford led decliners, losing 1.94 percent or 24 schillings to 1,215.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index added on 0.68 points, or 0.14 percent, to 478.55.
The June ATX future advanced 7.5 points to 1,312.6 on turnover of 3,324 contracts.
